newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June payrolls rise 217,000.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June payrolls rise 217,000.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported that payrolls rose by 217,000 in June compared to a revised 166,000 in May, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a payrolls rise of 222,000 for the month and a steady jobless rate of 4.8 percent.
DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "The numbers were actually pretty moderate."

"We got education jobs that inflated the (payrolls) number by perhaps roughly 50,000. The jobless rate is up to 5.0 percent ... all these numbers are fairly moderate and should give the (Treasury) bond market a little bit of support."

GARY THAYER, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT A. G. EDWARDS AND SONS INC: "Generally a good number that shows the economy is very healthy but not overheating. A gain of 217,000 is within the range that we've seen over the last 18 months or so, and the unemployment rate of 5.0 percent is still relatively low, even though it's an uptick from previous months.
"Its generally still a very good economy.
"The bond market likes it ... the dollar is relatively stable and this number confirms that the Fed really didn't need to raise rates this week."

CARY LEAHEY, CHIEF U.S. ECONOMIST, HIGH FREQUENCY ECONOMICS:"You are still looking at a change in jobs of over 200,000. It looks like 240,000 the past three months. How much longer can the markets and the Fed ignore very solid job growth which is helping boost consumer confidence to all time highs."
CHERYL KATZ, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH: "With the unemployment rate going up, it seems clear that economic growth has moderated to a more sustainable level.
"We continue to have very healthy non-inflationary growth, we continue to see a lack of wage pressure, and on top of that you are starting to get some looseneing of the job market.
"All in all the economy continues to grow at a much more sustainable pace."
